thesis: The credit belongs to the data, not the algorithm: no training trick won, and Alaska's own human-checked earthquake picks, recorded by 75 seafloor and 30 land seismometers, taught an existing AI picker to find roughly three times as many quakes, most of the gain far offshore.
supporting_facts: c11 no training strategy was substantially better
c12 local waveform data set improved performance
c14 roughly 3x more earthquakes than the analyst-checked catalog (this 2018-2019 catalog only)
c16 biggest gains far offshore and outer rise
falsifiability: False if a training trick clearly beat the others, if extra quakes scattered off known structure, or if gains were not concentrated offshore. Abstract says the opposite on all three. False-positive rate unknown (paper body unreachable).
counterpoint: Temporary 2018-2019 experiment, judged from an abstract with no absolute counts. Roughly 3x says nothing about whether seismicity rose or what a permanent network hears today. The expensive part (a dense seafloor array and hand-checked labels) came first. Open question: does Alaska keep putting sensors on the seafloor to feed the recipe?
second_movement: The headline reads AI breakthrough, the paper's own finding is data decided it. Credit moves to the people who deployed instruments and checked picks by hand.
